KINE 421.d: This course is a seminar style course that examines acute and chronic effects of exercise stimuli on physiological adaptation as relevant to health, disease and human performance. Topics will vary depending on current issues in exercise physiology. Examples include metabolism, fatigue, diabetes, genetics, muscular dystrophy, orthopedics, cancer and cardiovascular disease. The course is intended for those with a background in biology and/or physiology and interest in exercise and health.
KINE 421.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 375.d: Research experience for upperclassmen in the Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology major. Department Permission Required. Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 375.restr: Enrollment limited to students with a class of Junior or Senior. Enrollment is limited to students with a major in Sports Medicine & Exercise Phy. Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 499.d: Students will assist in conducting a course in which they have previously excelled. The student will learn techniques in course management, instruction, and evaluation. Department Permission Required. Recommended prerequisite(s): Junior or Senior standing, declared major in Sports Medicine & Exercise Physiology, and at least an "A-" in the course serving as the practicum. Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 499.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 302.d: An introduction to the discipline of mechanics as it applies to biological systems. Primary emphasis is placed on humans and other vertebrate species. Topics covered include the kinematics and kinetics of movement, material and functional properties of musculoskeletal tissues and the integration of musculoskeletal function from molecules and cells to whole animals. Recommended prerequisite(s): KINE 321.
KINE 302.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 441.d: This course will specifically address cardiac and skeletal muscle physiology and plasticity when introduced to various stimuli. These stimuli include exercise, aging, injury, altitude, microgravity, heat, and pharmacological agents. An emphasis will be placed on practical application to health, disease, and performance enhancement.
KINE 441.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 351.d: Study of the pro-sections and cadavers are used for learning and understanding human anatomy in a gross anatomy examination laboratory at BCM in the Texas Medical Center. Hands-on examination of human anatomy in this course provides supplemental practical experience for lectures in KINE 300, Human Anatomy courses.
KINE 351.restr: Enrollment is limited to students with a major in Health Sciences or Sports Medicine & Exercise Phy. Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 238.d: Topics and credit hours vary each semester. Contact department for current semester's topic(s). Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 238.type: Independent Study, Internship/Practicum, Laboratory, Lecture, Seminar, Activity Course, Lecture/Laboratory, Intensive Learning Experience, Research, Studio
KINE 238.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 455.d: This course examines how exercise and physical activity impact the human immune system, including the long term effects of exercise on aging and response to space flight. The course will explore how acute and chronic stressors, with a specific emphasis on exercise, can impact the immune system and overall health. Recommended Prerequisite(s): KINE 321
KINE 455.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 440.d: Designed to introduce students to research methods, statistical techniques, and topics appropriate for experimental research.
KINE 440.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 495.d: To provide the student with an opportunity to participate in a research project under the supervision of a Rice Kinesiology faculty member and/or an external researcher. Department Permission Required. Recommended Prerequisite(s): KINE 319 and KINE 440. Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 495.restr: Enrollment limited to students with a class of Junior or Senior. Enrollment is limited to students with a major in Sports Medicine & Exercise Phy. Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 275.d: Internship experience in Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology. Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 275.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 310.d: Examine the psychological foundations that underlie sport and exercise participation. Recommended Prerequisite(s): PSYC 101.
KINE 310.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 311.d: Designed to provide a basic understanding of the theories related to skill acquisition, development, and movement. Learners develop an understanding of the cognitive, behavioral, and neurological concepts needed to become skilled at movements. The course will also incorporate laboratory experiences in the physiological, neurological, and psychological factors of human movement.
KINE 311.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 321.d: This course examines the acute and chronic effects of exercise on physiological functions. Topics include nutrition, energy transfer, fatigue, metabolism, disease, aging, preventative medicine, genetics, elite performance, ergogenic aids, exercise testing, and specificity of training.
KINE 321.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 410.d: An advanced, multidisciplinary consideration of how humans perform. Class work will center around problem solving using a case study methodology.
KINE 410.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 301.d: This course will address the fundamental principles of human physiology at the cell, tissue, organ, organ system, and organism levels. Emphasis will be placed on mechanisms of function and homeostasis as achieved through the coordinated function of homeostatic control systems.
KINE 301.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 403.d: This course will address current scientific knowledge about common macronutrients, micronutrients, and supplements, and how they may enhance athletic performance. The course will also focus on the role of nutritional timing, volume, and periodization to achieve practical results in endurance, strength, power and speed. Recommended Prerequisite(s): KINE 300 and KINE 301 and KINE 321
KINE 403.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 120.d: An introduction to studies in the areas of human movement: anatomy and physiology, exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor learning and control, and psychological aspects of sport and exercise.
KINE 120.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 460.d: This course examines the science behind exercise testing and prescription. It applies the concepts of exercise physiology to complete exercise testing and develop exercise programs for various populations.

KINE 326.d: This course provides an epidemiological foundation to exercise and physical activity research related to public health. The course is designed to present evidence of the positive effects of physical activity and exercise in preventing disease, disability, and increasing quality of life.
KINE 326.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 498.d: This course is designed to provide students with a foundation of exercise testing and prescription. It will cover the many parameters of fitness assessment, including cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, and body composition. The course will incorporate both lectures and lab based activities. Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 498.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 300.d: An introduction to normal human anatomy structure and function. All major body systems will be examined in both lecture and laboratory format using a variety of physical and virtual models.
KINE 300.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 415.d: This course examines the psychological factors involved in sport-related injuries and the rehabilitation process. Topics include personal and situational factors influencing injury and recover, adherence to rehabilitation programs, social support, returning to play after injury, and the application of psychological interventions to optimize the recovery process. Recommended Prerequisite(s): KINE 310
KINE 415.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 490.d: Considers issues related to athletic injury including mechanisms, assessment, management, and rehabilitation.
KINE 490.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 320.d: This course provides a hands-on laboratory to demonstrate and apply in-depth human physiology concepts. Students will collect, analyze, and report data on physiological variables. Findings will be applied to key human physiology concepts including homeostasis, isolated and integrated functions of body systems, and response to activity and exercise.
KINE 320.restr: Enrollment is limited to students with a major in Sports Medicine & Exercise Phy. Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 430.d: Upper level course designed to provide students with practical application of basic science knowledge obtained in lower level courses within the department of Kinesiology. The course will address the management of common sports injuries from time of injury to return to play. At the end of the course, students will have a comprehensive understanding of athletic injuries and their management.
KINE 430.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 477.d: Topics and credit hours may vary each semester. Contact department for current semester's topic(s). Repeatable for Credit.
KINE 477.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 419.d: This course offers an in-depth look into selected developmental, degenerative, and hyperkinetic movement disorders resulting in abnormal muscle tone and/or motor control. Multiple aspects of each disorder (presentation, treatment, and progression) will be considered through a variety of sources.
KINE 419.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 319.d: Topics include displaying and describing data, the normal curve, regression, statistical inference including parametric and non-parametric analyses, and hypothesis testing. Students also have the opportunity to analyze data using SPSS and Excel software.
KINE 319.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

KINE 412.d: Exploration of the neurophysiological, behavioral, and biomechanical aspects of human movement and development.
KINE 412.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.
